content:
alex: quick heads-up — after the KV priming tweak yesterday I'm seeing a small class of decode-only spikes. p95 prefill looks fine but p99 decode jumps for ~2-3% of traffic.

maria: can you drop the perf snapshot / example IDs?

alex: pasted a short sample from traces:
```
trace_id: t-9843
model: llama-13b-qlora
request: tokens=512, prompt_len=64
prefill: p95=48ms p99=82ms
decode: p95=120ms p99=410ms (spike cohort)
kv_state: cold-to-warm within 1-3 requests
kernel: selected="cutlass_fp16" vs expected="gemm_fwd_int8"
```

raj: interesting — kernel flip + KV warmup smells like the scheduler is batching these requests into a decode-heavy path and losing kernel affinity. Could be the token-budget threshold being hit and forcing a different kernel selection.

sam: fwiw I noticed the queue policy change we merged (cohort-shepherd routing) biases short prefill requests into the same lane as long decode flows. That increases cache pressure and sometimes triggers the fallback kernel with worse perf.

leah: proposal: add a soft split that routes by phase-likelihood instead of fixed cohort tag. Keep prefill batches isolated for first 150ms of enqueueing so KV gets primed and kernel selector stabilizes. Also tweak decode token_budget target down to 6 for bursty streams.

maria: SGTM. Can you mock config?

alex: putting a small canary config here to test on prod-cc1 0.5% traffic:
```yaml
batching:
  phase_aware_split: true
  prefill_window_ms: 150
  decode_window_ms: 20
  token_budget_targets:
    prefill: 128
    decode: 6
kernel_selector:
  prefer_affine: true
  stable_select_threshold_ms: 200
kv:
  priming_grace_ms: 300
```

sam: will roll canary at 00:05 UTC. monitor p50/p95/p99 for decode, and kernel churn metric (kernel_select_count).

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/scheduler-phase-split -> prod-cc1 (0.5%)

alex: thanks. I'll attach the trace link and a quick dashboard (p99 decode, kernel_select_count, kv_miss_rate) — https://dash.internal/r/eng-runtime/scheduler-shepherd

raj: one more thought: add an ephemeral KV priming path that sends a 1-2 token micro-prefill for sessions that look cold before joining decode batches. Low cost but helps keep the KV hot.

leah: agree. if canary looks good, we should run it for 24h and then A/B with a shorter prefill window (100ms) to find the sweet spot.

alex: noted. I'll capture a couple of sample trace IDs and open a follow-up postmortem if we see regressions.

maria: thanks team — ping me if any alerts fire during the canary. :thumbsup:
